title: ERR_BUG (_payload.data_left() < (int)p.size) with WebSocketPeer call from another thread on Web
body: ### Tested versions - Reproducible in 4.7.2 and master branch (commit 4b03d555837093ea1e3ca1d28eda4c73534e0fe7) ### System information Godot v4.8.dev.custom_build Web Build configuration: Emscripten 6.0.9, multi-threaded, no GDExtension support. ### Issue description When using WebSocket peer from another thread, the web build sometimes produces the following error: ``` ERROR: Condition "_payload.data_left() < (int)p.size" is true. Returning: ERR_BUG at: read_packet (modules\websocket\packet_buffer.h:85) GDScript backtrace (most recent call first): [0] _socket_network_worker (res://client.gd:63) ERROR: Condition "err != OK" is true. Returning: err at: get_packet (modules\websocket\emws_peer.cpp:149) GDScript backtrace (most recent call first): [0] _socket_network_worker (res://client.gd:63) ``` From my understanding this is some sort of a race condition, because the bug appears conditionally, based on the amount and size of data being sent, as well as the size of the socket buffers. ### Additional info This patch from my colleague is related: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/112453 But after digging it myself, I am not sure this is a proper fix and not a workaround. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Spam the websocket peer with packets from some server (e.g. python one from the MRP) 2. Work with WebSocketPeer from non-main GDScript thread (call `get_packet()`) For the MRP: 1. Download the project and the export templates. 2. Export the project to the web_buggy fodler in the project root 3. Run run_buggy script: it will launch a python server and launch the godot app in the browser 4. The Dev console will have the mentioned ERR_BUG message ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) The project: [err_bug_test_proj.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31833346/err_bug_test_proj.zip) Export templates (put into the project folder): (With the master branch commit) [template_buggy.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31832929/template_buggy.zip) (With a fix/workaround, that adds mutex for EMWS peer, not related to the mentioned PR with workaround, but it works too) [template_fixed.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31832937/template_fixed.zip)
